key_insight: Electron beam welding can successfully reconstruct Charpy impact specimens for reactor-pressure-vessel steels, producing dense weld zones with no obvious cracking and preserving near-original mechanical performance, especially for 10Cr12Ni3Mo2VN.
engineering_relevance: This supports specimen reconstitution for nuclear materials qualification, reducing the need for full-size test material while maintaining confidence in impact and hardness assessments.
method: Electron-beam welded restructured Charpy specimens for 16MND5, 10Cr12Ni3Mo2VN, and X6NiCrTiMoVB 25-15-2 steels.
Evaluated weld quality and microstructure using non-destructive flaw detection, optical microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy.
Measured Vickers hardness and impact toughness to compare restructured specimens with original specimens.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dense weld-zone microstructures without obvious cracks, and the 10Cr12Ni3Mo2VN specimens showed the best weld quality with properties closest to the originals.
watch_item: Results are limited to the tested specimen types and conditions, so broader applicability requires validation across more steels, weld parameters, and service-relevant loading conditions.
paper_title: Effects of electron beam welding on the microstructure and impact properties of three reconstituted steels
